user.title: Eni Plenitude customer area
user.description: The credentials you use on eniplenitude.com/my-eni. The password is used only when the session (30 days) expires.

data_description.email: Email of your Eni Plenitude customer account.
data_description.password: Stored in Home Assistant and sent only to the Plenitude login service.

supply.title: Supply
supply.description: The account has more than one electricity supply: choose the one to import. Add the integration again for the others.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in to Plenitude again
reauth_confirm.description: Plenitude refused the login for {email}: enter the password again.

error.invalid_auth: Credentials refused by Plenitude (or an additional verification is required).
error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the Plenitude customer area (the reason is in the Home Assistant log).
error.no_supplies: The account has no electricity supply with the consumption analysis.
error.supply_missing: The configured supply is no longer in this account.
error.unknown: Unexpected error: see the Home Assistant log.
error.portal_refused: Plenitude accepted the login, but the customer area refuses the data of the account. Check that the customer area works in a browser, then try again later. If it keeps happening, turn on the debug log (see the README) and open an issue.

init.title: Energy price
init.description: Plenitude does not expose the price of the offer: enter it to get the cost too. If you change it, the cost of the whole history is recomputed. Other costs (fixed fees, power fee, TV licence, charges per kWh) are added with **Add cost** in the integration page.

prices.title: Prices per kWh
prices.description: Prices of the energy in euro per kWh, as in your offer, with a comma or a point for the decimals. Charges per kWh that are not in these prices (transport, system charges, excise duty) can be added as costs per kWh.

data_description.price: Euro per kWh, the same in every hour.
data_description.price_f1: Euro per kWh, Monday to Friday 8:00-19:00.
data_description.price_f2: Euro per kWh, Monday to Friday 7:00-8:00 and 19:00-23:00, Saturday 7:00-23:00.
data_description.price_f3: Euro per kWh, nights 23:00-7:00, Sundays and holidays.
data_description.price_f23: Euro per kWh in every hour outside F1.

error.invalid_price: Enter a price between 0 and 10 euro per kWh, with a comma or a point for the decimals (at most 6), without thousands separators.

costo_ultimo_giorno.name: Consumption cost of the last day

login_refused.message: Plenitude refused the login ({error}): sign in again.

analysis_unavailable.message: The consumption analysis is not available for the configured supply.

supply_missing.message: The configured supply is no longer in the Plenitude account.

portal_refused.message: The customer area refuses the data of the account: signing in again in a few minutes

user.title: Add a cost
user.description: A cost of your contract besides the price of the energy. Monthly, two-monthly, yearly and per kW per month costs count in full in the cards; costs per kWh and percentages (VAT, for example) are in the cost of every hour, also in the Energy dashboard. The amount comes in the next step.

data_description.name: Any text, for example: TV licence, fixed fee, power fee, system charges, VAT.
data_description.kind: How it is charged: every month, every two months, every year, every month for each kW of the contract power (power fee), for each kWh consumed, or as a percentage of the rest of the bill (VAT, for example).

data_description.name: Any text, for example: TV licence, fixed fee, power fee, system charges, VAT.
data_description.kind: How it is charged: every month, every two months, every year, every month for each kW of the contract power (power fee), for each kWh consumed, or as a percentage of the rest of the bill (VAT, for example).

data_description.amount: Euro (euro per kWh for the costs per kWh), with a comma or a point for the decimals (at most 6). Use a negative amount for a discount.
data_description.exempt: Turn it on if the percentages do not apply to this cost: for example the TV licence, which pays no VAT in the bill.

per_kw.title: Amount per kW and power
per_kw.description: **{name}** is charged every month for each kW of the contract power: the bill shows it as committed power (potenza impegnata). The customer area's value is suggested when it is known.

data_description.amount: Euro per kW per month, with a comma or a point for the decimals (at most 6).
data_description.exempt: Turn it on if the percentages do not apply to this cost: for example the TV licence, which pays no VAT in the bill.

percent.title: Percentage
percent.description: **{name}** is a percentage of the energy price and of every cost not excluded, for example VAT at 10%. Percentages do not apply to each other. Excise duties are an amount per kWh in the bill: enter them as a cost per kWh, so that the percentage applies to them too.

data_description.amount: For example 10 for 10%, with a comma or a point for the decimals (at most 6). Negative for a discount.

error.invalid_number: Enter a number, with a comma or a point for the decimals (for example 9,15 or 9.15), without thousands separators.
error.out_of_range: The amount must be between -100000 and 100000 euro.
error.invalid_power: Enter a power between 0.1 and 999 kW, with a comma or a point for the decimals (at most 6).
error.invalid_percent: Enter a percentage between -100 and 100, with a comma or a point for the decimals (at most 6).
